To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TRIzol RNA extraction protocol is recommended for HIV-1 RNA extraction from plasma.

the Chomczynsky method gave the best results, but the single-step methods are easier to perform and are sensitive enough to be used for the extraction of RNA from the plasma of HIV-1 infected patients.
the extraction method described by Chomcynski and Sacch (1987) gave the best results, followed by the single-step methods of TRIzol and NASBA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of eight different methods of HIV-1-RNA extraction, in order to find a rapid method for the detection of low copy numbers of viral RNA in plasma.
the isolation of HIV-RNA from plasma.
the development of methods for the detection of HIV RNA in the plasma of patients with AIDS and AIDS-related complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TRIzol and the NASBA methods are the most appropriate for the extraction of RNA from plasma for the detection of HIV-1 by RT-PCR.
the Chomczynki and Sacchi method is the most sensitive method and the TRIzol and NASBA methods are the most practical and rapid methods for HIV-1 RNA extraction.
for most of the extraction methods evaluated the inter-assay variation is within acceptable limits, but for the extraction of a large series of samples, single-step methods are to be preferred.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extraction method that gave the most reliable results by RT- PCR was the Chomczynsky method.

the method described by Chomzynski and Sacchii (1987) is the most sensitive, but that the TRIzol (Gibco BRL) method is a rapid, reliable alternative for the extraction of RNA from plasma for the detection of HIV-1-RNA by NASBA.
for the isolation of HIV RNA from plasma, the TRIzol and the NASBA methods offer a rapid and sensitive alternative to the guanidine method.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the method described by Chomcynski and Sacchii is the most reliable method for HIV RNA extraction, but the TRIzol extraction method and the extraction method offered in the NASBA kit are also good alternatives.
